newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber keeps focus on Goodyear Tire.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber keeps focus on Goodyear Tire.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market remained quiet by midday on Wednesday while the trade cast a worried look on the strike by 13,000 workers in Goodyear Tire, dealers said.
"People are still watching the strike in Goodyear. We're beginning to hear talk from the U.S. that Goodyear may be forced to defer receiving shipments of rubber," a trader said.
Dealers said news the Thai government was seeking 10,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber had no impact in the market.
"I don't think the Thai government's move will help the market much at the moment," another dealer said.
One impact of the strike is the sinking offer price for SIR20 rubber, which dipped this morning to 46.5 U.S. cents a lb against yesterday's quote of around 47 cents a lb.
Traders said Pirelli was supposed to have recently clinched a deal for several hundred tonnes of SMR20 rubber.
"We didn't see any deals done this morning, however. It's very quiet," one dealer said.
At around 0430 GMT, June RSS3 was indicated at 106.75 U.S. cents a kg from 107.75 cents. June RSS1 was indicated at 154.50 Singapore cents (US$1.07) a kg from 155.00 cents.
